description: The opaque parts are chosen over the whole derivation, and a %opaque constituent that the choice leaves out is ordinary, even when a token is emitted over it (engine §11). The first `inner` lies inside the opaque part `outer`, whose rule has no emission clause. So the walk reaches it and its own emission runs. The second lies inside the opaque part `held`, whose capture item emits a token over it. Each token has the source of its input token and sounds `b`, not `?`. `skipped` lies inside `gone`, which emits ε, so the walk does not reach it, and it emits nothing. It is no opaque part, so it takes in no text, and `tail`, the next opaque part, takes the space before it.
grammar:
%rule text (outer held gone tail)
%rule outer :- $.verbatim-text | (A inner)

%rule held :- $.verbatim-text | $i:inner %emits $i :: J


%rule inner :- $.verbatim-text | B %emits $ :: I


%rule gone skipped %erased

%rule skipped :- $.verbatim-text | C %emits $ :: S


%rule tail :- $.verbatim-text | D %emits $ :: T
